# #4614 — triage notes

**Issue:** [#4614](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/4614)
"Assert/hang in SROA_HLSL pass related to empty base struct regression",
filed 2022-08-24 by `simontaylor81`, open, labelled `crash`.

**Ground truth:** `main-debug`, dxc 1.9.0.5433, public commit `13730886e`.
(The local Debug binary self-reports a different, fork-local commit in its
version string; `13730886e` is the publicly resolvable commit the source
corresponds to and the one cited everywhere here.)

**Verdict:** `repros`, `always-repro'd` across all 20 stable releases
v1.4.1907 (2019-07) … v1.9.2607 plus `main-debug`. The word "regression" in
the title is not supported by measurement — see *History*.

---

## 1. The repro is the reporter's, unmodified

`repro.hlsl` is byte-identical to the fenced block in the issue body **and** to
the source stored behind the Compiler Explorer link a maintainer posted on the
issue in 2024 (`godbolt.org/z/7zW3febaj`). Checked mechanically rather than by
eye — all three normalise to sha256 `ded14f5e…679b09`
(`manual-case-fidelity.txt`, generated by `gen-fidelity.py`). Arguments are the
issue's own `-E main -T vs_6_0`; `cmd.txt` reorders them only.

Repro quality: **complete**. Nothing was reconstructed, no flag was added or
removed, no profile was changed.

## 2. The predicate: one defect, two signatures

`match.json` is

```json
{ "kind": "any_of", "value": [ { "kind": "timeout" }, { "kind": "internal_failure" } ] }
```

The title says "Assert/hang"; the predecessor issue #3016 says why those are
one thing: *"an assert (which manifests as a hang outside of the debugger)"*.

This is not a theoretical precaution — it is what the measurements show:

| build class | count | signature observed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stable release binaries (Release, `NDEBUG`) | 20 / 20 | **hang** — no output, killed at the 60s timeout |
| `main-debug` (assert-enabled) | 1 / 1 | **internal failure** — `0xE0000001`, "Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert" |

So **each clause carries exactly the builds the other one misses**
(`manual-case-release-matrix.txt`):

- a bare `internal_failure` predicate scores all **20** release binaries as
  clean, and reports `never-repro'd-in-releases`;
- a bare `timeout` predicate scores `main-debug` as clean, and reports
  `does-not-repro` on ground truth.

Either alone reports this open, always-reproducing defect as fixed. Neither
signature is the symptom on its own; failing to compile a valid shader is.

Deliberately **not** keyed to the assert message — SKILL.md records that the
text varies by build and platform, and that an internal failure may print
nothing at all. Nor to exit status alone: note in the matrix that a timed-out
run records `# exit: 0`, so anything shaped like `nonzero_exit` would score
every hang as a *successful compile*.

## 3. Ground truth: where it fails

`out-main-debug.txt` — exit `0xE0000001`, stderr `Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert`.

`manual-case-assert-stack.txt` (generated by `gen-assert-stack.py`) has the
detail, and it is the same place #3016's 2020 stack named:

```
Error: assert(0 && "Type mismatch.")
File:
<repo>\lib\Transforms\Scalar\ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp(2690)
Func:	`anonymous-namespace'::SROA_Helper::RewriteBitCast
...
02 dxcompiler!`anonymous namespace'::SROA_Helper::RewriteBitCast+0x788
03 dxcompiler!`anonymous namespace'::SROA_Helper::RewriteForScalarRepl+0x286
04 dxcompiler!`anonymous namespace'::SROA_Helper::DoScalarReplacement+0xd20
05 dxcompiler!`anonymous namespace'::SROAGlobalAndAllocas+0xa48
06 dxcompiler!`anonymous namespace'::SROA_Parameter_HLSL::runOnModule+0x8a7
```

The innermost three frames are exactly #3016's. The two outer frames differ —
#3016 reached the helper through `SROA_HLSL::performScalarRepl` /
`SROA_HLSL::runOnFunction`, today it is reached through `SROAGlobalAndAllocas`
/ `SROA_Parameter_HLSL::runOnModule` — which matches the reporter's 2022
description, *"callstack looked basically the same"*.

## 4. Why the assert and the hang are the same defect

This is the part worth reading, because it is what makes the composed
predicate correct rather than merely cautious.

**Measured.** Case B of `manual-case-assert-stack.txt` continues *past* the
first assert with cdb's `gh` ("go handled"), which per SKILL.md emulates
`NDEBUG` — it runs the code a Release build would have run. The very next
thing that happens is DXC's **own loop detector** firing:

```
Error: 	!(&TheUse != PrevUse)
File:
<repo>\lib\Transforms\Scalar\ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp(2996)
Func:	`anonymous-namespace'::SROA_Helper::RewriteForScalarRepl.
	Infinite loop while SROA'ing value, use isn't getting eliminated.
```

**Corroborated from source.** Both guards are compiled out under `NDEBUG`:

- `ScalarReplAggregatesHLSL.cpp:2690` is a plain `assert(0 && "Type mismatch.")`
  immediately followed by `return;` (line 2691). With the assert gone, the
  function returns having left the bitcast use in place;
- `RewriteForScalarRepl` loops `while (!V->use_empty())` and guards progress
  with `DXASSERT_LOCALVAR(PrevUse, &TheUse != PrevUse, "Infinite loop while
  SROA'ing value, …")` at line 2994. Under `NDEBUG` that macro expands to
  `do { (void)(local); } while (0)` (`include/dxc/Support/Global.h:362`).

So in a release build the loop re-selects the same use forever with nothing to
stop it. That is the reported hang, and it is a *consequence* of the condition
the first assert detects.

This is the discriminator SKILL.md requires before writing "silent by
construction" — and it comes out the opposite way. This is **not** an
`NDEBUG` artefact: compiling the asserts out does not silence the defect, it
converts a fast failure into an unbounded one.

**Confirmed in a real release build.** `manual-case-hang-evidence.txt`
(generated by `gen-hang-evidence.py`) runs the v1.9.2607 release binary on the
repro for 300 s — 5× the triage timeout — with no output and no exit, and
samples every thread's stack at t=30 s and t=90 s.

The two samples are the same stack. Frames 02–17 are byte-identical *including
their Child-SP values*, and the two innermost frames differ only by a 62-byte
return-address offset inside the same function
(`…+0x3c0954` → `…+0x3c0992`). Sixty seconds of execution at a fixed stack
depth, cycling within one function, is a spin — a merely slow compile would
show the stack moving. (The shipped release binary has no symbols available,
so its frames resolve only as `dxcompiler!DxcCreateInstance2+<offset>`; the
named frames come from the Debug build in §3.)

## 5. Controls

Four, all declared with `--expect no-match`, all clean (exit 0):

| control | what it changes | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `control-not-empty.hlsl` | uncomments the reporter's own `float makeMeNotEmpty;` | compiles |
| `control-no-assign.hlsl` | removes the reporter's other documented workaround line | compiles |
| `control-no-inherit.hlsl` | holds `BaseStruct` as a **member** instead of a base | compiles |
| `control-simplified-3016.hlsl` | the regression test added by the commit that closed #3016 | compiles |

The first two are the two workarounds the reporter wrote into the shader's
comments, and they behave as he described. The third isolates the trigger to
the **base-class** relationship, which matches his own hypothesis —
*"something related to the clang empty-base-class optimisation, which makes the
struct layouts of the base and child look different"*. The fourth matters for
§6.

Together they establish the predicate discriminates: it does not fire on any
`vs_6_0` compile, on any shader containing an empty struct, or on any shader
containing this struct hierarchy — only on the reported construct.

## 6. History — and why the title's "regression" is not supported

`bisect --linear`, deliberately: the issue is an explicit fix-then-reappear
(#3016 closed 2021-06-24, same shader reported broken again 2022-08-23), so
the symptom cannot be assumed monotonic and binary search would be unsound —
worse, it short-circuits on agreeing endpoints, which here would have skipped
the entire middle of the history where any fix window would live.

**Every one of the 20 stable releases reproduces**, v1.4.1907 (2019-07)
through v1.9.2607, plus `main-debug`. No invalid probes: no build emitted a
diagnostic, and a build that rejected the shader could not have satisfied
either clause of the predicate. 5 probeable prereleases and 1 release with no
usable `dxc` asset were excluded by policy and are named in the bisect output.

There is therefore **no regression window in any shipped release**. The
relevant history is instead:

- `527d58e5a` ("Handles empty embedded struct as first field of struct.",
  PR #3827, 2021-06-24) says `Fixes #3016` and is the commit on whose merge
  #3016 was closed the same day;
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor 527d58e5a <tag>`, run against all 20 tags in
  the scan, first answers "contained" at **v1.6.2106** and answers
  "not contained" for v1.4.1907 / v1.5.2010 / v1.6.2104
  (`manual-case-fix-ancestry.txt`, generated by `gen-fix-ancestry.py`). Both
  directions are recorded there on purpose: a test that never changes its
  answer would not establish a boundary;
- **v1.6.2106 hangs on this repro** (`out-v1.6.2106.txt`), as does every
  release after it.

That commit changed `SROA_Parameter_HLSL::flattenArgument` (semantic
inheritance for zero-sized fields), not `RewriteBitCast`, and the test it
added — `tools/clang/test/HLSLFileCheck/hlsl/types/struct/embeddedEmptyStruct.hlsl`
— is a struct with an empty first member returned from `main`, with no base
class and no empty-struct assignment. That test's shader still compiles
cleanly today (`variant-simplified-3016-main-debug.txt`).

pow2clk anticipated exactly this on #3016 in 2022:
*"I guess that's what I get for including my simplified version instead of the
original repro in the test suite."*

**Scope of the claim.** This says the *repro in the issue* never compiled in
any probeable release. It does **not** say the reporter was wrong about his own
codebase: he described applying a local workaround and then meeting the defect
"in a different place", which is consistent with a genuine new occurrence in a
shader that is not this one. What is measurable here is that the attached
repro has no clean release.

Correspondingly, v1.4.1907 is the bisection floor (oldest release with a usable
`dxc`), so "always" means "for as long as it is possible to check" — 2019-07
onward, which predates #3016's 2020-07 filing by a year.

## 7. Compiler Explorer

<https://godbolt.org/z/erb45rxTb> — `dxc_1_6_2112` and `dxc_trunk`, both with
`-T vs_6_0 -E main`. Both panes end in
`Killed - processing time exceeded / Program terminated with signal: SIGKILL`
(exit 143), i.e. the hang, on a public third-party service and on two
independent build ages. Full pane text in `manual-case-godbolt-verify.txt`;
the shortlink was read back through the CE API and confirmed to hold both
panes, the right arguments and the banner.

Note this is an unusually informative CE link for a crash issue: SKILL.md's
standing caveat is that CE runs Release builds so asserts look clean there.
Here the Release manifestation is the loud one, so CE shows the defect rather
than hiding it. The maintainer's own 2024 link shows the same thing with one
pane.

## 8. Labels

Now: `crash` — accurate and kept.

Proposed additions:

- **`type-system`** ("Bugs relating to inconsistencies in HLSL's type system").
  The failing assert is literally `"Type mismatch."`, on a struct-layout
  disagreement between a derived type and its empty base.
- **`test`** ("Test issues or more test coverage needed"). Evidence-backed
  rather than a hunch: the regression test shipped with the fix that closed
  #3016 compiles cleanly today while the reported shader does not, and the
  maintainer had already identified that gap in the thread.

No removals. `bug` was considered and left out as redundant with `crash`;
`low-hanging-fruit` and `rca` were considered and rejected as claims about
effort or process that this evidence cannot support.

## 9. Suggested action

`still-valid-keep-open`. It reproduces everywhere, the repro is complete and
minimal, and the only new information triage can add is the history: there is
no regression to bisect, and a fix needs to address `SROA_Helper::RewriteBitCast`
rather than the path `527d58e5a` corrected. A fix should take the issue's own
shader as its test.

## 10. Limits of this triage

- The 60 s timeout proves "no result in 60 s"; the 300 s run proves "no result
  in 300 s". Unbounded non-termination is established from the source
  (`while (!V->use_empty())` with the progress guard compiled out), not from
  wall-clock alone.
- Release-build behaviour was measured on shipped binaries and reproduced from
  the Debug build via `gh`; no Release build was compiled locally.
- The attribution of #3016's closure to `527d58e5a` is direct — the commit says
  `Fixes #3016` — but "this commit did not fix the attached repro" is a
  statement about the repro's behaviour in v1.6.2106, not a claim about what
  the author intended to fix.
- Whether the reporter's *production* shader regressed between 2021 and 2022 is
  not measurable from here; only the attached repro was tested.
- Determinism was not separately stress-tested, but nothing here rests on a
  single observation: `main-debug` asserted on all three independent
  invocations (the harness run plus both debugger cases), and v1.9.2607 hung on
  both of its two independent runs (the release scan and the 300 s run). The
  mechanism — a loop that re-selects the same use — is deterministic by
  construction, so `--repeat` was not used.
